exercise.name: Lever Decline Chest Press

reference.title: Lever Decline Chest Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Decline chest press machine (selectorized, iso-lateral lever arms)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the handles come back, breathe out as you press forward and down.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s back, short pause, about 1.3 s press

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can press with the back on the pad and the shoulders down.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Sit tall with the back on the pad and the feet flat; set the seat so the handles start level with the lower chest; arms extended forward and down, palms down.
Breathe in and let the handles come back and up toward the lower chest on their arc, elbows tucked about 45 degrees.
Pause with the hands beside the lower ribs; shoulders down and back on the pad.
Breathe out and press forward and down along the arc until the arms are long.
Squeeze the lower chest with the arms long and pointing down; keep the back on the pad.

mistakes.mistake: Seat too low or too high
mistakes.fix: Set the seat so the handles line up with the chest line the machine is built for.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about 45-60 degrees from the trunk.

mistakes.mistake: Back leaving the pad to push
mistakes.fix: Keep the back and head on the pad; lighten the load.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders rolling forward at the end
mistakes.fix: Stop with the arms long and the shoulder blades still on the pad.

kinematics.peak: ≈131° with the hands beside the lower chest
kinematics.norm: From well bent with the hands beside the chest to nearly straight (clinical opinion)
About 45-60 degrees from the trunk at the chest (clinical opinion)
Pronated: palms down on horizontal handles (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pivot 160.5 cm high; hands end 30 cm below the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Lever swings 16.9°; hands within 0.78 cm of the arc
kinematics.norm: The handles ride a decline arc: forward and down from the lower chest (clinical opinion)
Back on the pad, little trunk work compared with free-weight or standing presses (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012)
Seat set so the handles start at the lower chest, feet flat (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pause 0.5 s with the arms extended
kinematics.peak: 2 s back, 0.3 s pause, 1.3 s press
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s back and 1-1.5 s press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11201, Lever Decline Chest Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Load is user-chosen: start light and press without the back leaving the pad.
At the end of the set let the handles come back under control before letting go.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: shorten the range so the hands stop in front of the chest.
Low back discomfort: keep both feet flat and the back on the pad.
progressions: Slower return with a pause at the chest.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Prime mover; the downward press path favours the sternal and costal fibres (clinical opinion). Unstable presses activated the pectoralis about as much as machine work in one study (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Prime mover; the downward press path favours the sternal and costal fibres (clinical opinion). Unstable presses activated the pectoralis about as much as machine work in one study (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Moves the shoulder blade forward at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Moves the shoulder blade forward at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.core: Little demand with the back on the pad (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Controls the elbow on the return.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Controls the elbow on the return.

phases.label: Handles back to the lower chest

guides.label: Forward and down along the arc
